name: IL-09
label: Safe D

key_factors: Open seat after Schakowsky's retirement, but Democratic nominee Biss is well-funded
Republican candidate has minimal reported fundraising
Prediction markets price Democratic win near 95%
model.rationale: The seat's D+19 partisan lean and a well-funded Democratic nominee in Daniel Biss make a Democratic hold overwhelmingly likely, and markets price the race around 95% Democratic. The Republican nominee's lack of visible fundraising leaves little evidence of a serious challenge.
model.watch: Any late polling showing Biss underperforming the district's lean, or a surge of outside spending against him, would be the main signal to watch.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.
Open seat: Jan Schakowsky (D) is not on the ballot.

overview:
Jan Schakowsky's retirement leaves this Chicago-area seat open, but the district's D+19 partisan lean keeps it firmly in Democratic hands on paper. State Senator Daniel Biss enters the general election with roughly $2.9 million raised and outside groups active on both sides, while Republican John Elleson shows little reported fundraising or outside support.

With no public general-election polling, the forecast rests on fundamentals: the district's strong lean, Biss's financial advantage, and prediction markets pricing a Democratic win near 95%. The seat is rated Safe Democratic, with the open-seat transition the only source of added uncertainty.
